text:
ops-bot: [ALERT] 03:42 UTC — elevated 503s from kv-cache region eu-west-1. Pager triggered (P2). Rate: 12% 503s over 5m. Autochecks: node-flap=false, disk=OK, network=OK

maria: seeing the same in Grafana. p95 latency up from 45ms -> 230ms for embeddings endpoints in eu-west.

sam: assigning primary/secondary for the next 8h: primary = maria (taking immediate), secondary = sam (standby). lee will handle customer comms if needed. sylvia is on observability.

maria: quick triage — looks correlated with a burst of cold-starts on a host pool (pool-eu-emb-03). KV cache hitrate dropped 37% -> 12%.

sylvia: adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-evictions — follow section 2.3 for pool-level mitigation.

maria: what I did so far: cycled 2 nodes in pool-eu-emb-03, increased target replicas from 4 -> 6 for the pool, and disabled preemptions for that nodegroup. saw partial recovery in one availability zone.

sam: nice. any noisy customers? which clients are spiking?

maria: logs show a single customer shard (cust-omega) increased traffic 5x from 03:30. Might be a jobs spike. I filtered logs:
```
curl -s "https://logs.internal/query" -d 'service:embeddings region:eu-west client:cust-omega | count by minute'
# returns 300 -> 1500 QPS at 03:31
```

lee: I'm on standby for customer-facing messages. Drafting a short note: "We're investigating elevated errors in eu-west embeddings; temporary mitigation in progress; no long-term data loss; working on root cause. Will update in 30m."

sylvia: observability note: set a temporary alert: `eu-west-embeddings-503 > 5% for 5m` to avoid noisy flapping.

maria: also applied a per-pool KV cache size increase: updated config map kv-cache.max_entries=1.5x for pool-eu-emb-03. Need to watch memory headroom.

sam: any risk of OOMs after increasing cache?

maria: I checked metrics: memory headroom is 28% pre-change; after change ~18%. Acceptable for now.

ops-bot: [INFO] Runbook step completed: pool-scaling triggered by user. Recording action: increased replicas in pool-eu-emb-03.

maria: current status at 04:05 UTC: 503 rate down to 3.2%, p95 latency 110ms. Progressing.

sam: good. Primary/secondary note for next shift — Maria remains primary until 07:00 UTC. After that, onboarding for graveyard: night primary = alina (FYI, not on this thread). There's a potential coverage gap from 07:00-09:00 UTC if alina is not available — we need a volunteer or run automated scaling policies to hold.

lee: action item: I'll post a canned customer status at 04:15: include mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery.

sylvia: follow-up items for post-mortem: capture cust-omega traffic pattern, verify autoscaling thresholds didn't misfire, and check node churn logs. I'll create a ticket.

maria: one more precaution — set a temporary routing rule to route embeddings requests from cust-omega to the secondary pool `pool-eu-emb-fallback` until we confirm stable behavior. Applying now:
```
POST /routing/policies/apply
{ "match": "client:cust-omega and endpoint:embeddings", "route_to": "pool-eu-emb-fallback", "ttl": 1800 }
```

ops-bot: [ACTION] Routing policy applied by maria.

sam: summary for handoff notes:
- incident start: 03:42 UTC, elevated 503s in eu-west embeddings
- root cause (suspected): sudden traffic spike from cust-omega causing cache pressure and cold-starts on pool-eu-emb-03
- mitigations applied: scaled pool replicas 4->6, increased kv-cache entries, cycled 2 nodes, applied routing rule to fallback pool, temporary alert threshold adjusted
- current status: 503s reduced to 3.2%, p95 latency improving; customers impacted: partial errors for cust-omega only; broad customer impact resolved
- follow-ups: create postmortem ticket, determine autoscaler tuning, confirm fallback pool capacity, review job cadence for cust-omega

maria: next steps for incoming shift (copy into handoff): monitor eu-west 503s, confirm fallback pool steady-state, keep temporary alert for 30m, remove routing rule only after stable 15m window of <1% 503s.

sam: i'm logging the handoff now. If anyone takes over earlier, ping me. I will also note the potential coverage gap 07:00-09:00 and loop in ops rotation.

lee: posted customer note. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5864009876 (internal).

sylvia: creating postmortem ticket: https://phabricator/internal/T12345 — assigning to triage.

maria: thanks all. leaving detailed step list in the runbook thread. Primary remains on until 07:00 UTC. Secondary standing by. :thumbsup:

sam: ack, thanks. Closing this thread for now — will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
